sonnet.problem: Card 11 already asked about the LORD being on high above the roar of the waters. Card 12 re-asks the same fact and gives it away in the question ('the LORD on high is majestic above all that roar'). It also states a conclusion ('the LORD is greater than the mightiest waters') that the text doesn't say. Its wrong answer 'younger' is a different kind of answer from the comparison of strength the question sets up.
sonnet.rule: An easy follow-up asks something new. It never re-asks the same fact. Two lines that make the same point get one question.

sonnet.problem: The true/false statement repeats the answer to card 15 (holiness adorns the LORD's house), which the baker has just seen. Only 'for all the days to come' is new.
sonnet.rule: A True statement never just repeats the card before it.

sonnet.problem: Card 1 quotes 'The LORD reigns!' just before the question. That sets up the 'king' answer, which makes the choice easy to reason out before it is asked. The text says 'robed in majesty' and never says 'king' or 'royal robes'.
sonnet.rule: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.
